loading:
IMPORT MAP: keep the one existing import map at index.html line 9, in the head and before any script that imports anything. Browsers allow only one import map and it must come before the first module load, so add nothing there. It pins three@0.170.0 build/three.module.min.js and the examples/jsm/ addons. r170 supports WebGL2 only, so 3D requires canvas.getContext('webgl2'). Don't rely on the slLoad3D() probe alone: it also accepts webgl1.

SEQUENCE (everything lazy; nothing loads until the island tab opens):
1. slOpenWorld calls the slLoadWorld chain, which loads world-core.js, world-art.js, world-look.js (new and tiny) and rewards-world.js, and injects <link rel=stylesheet href=world/island-encore.css?v=N>. render() draws the existing 2D SVG island immediately, as it does today.
2. After the first 2D draw, rewards-world calls maybeBoot3D(). It does nothing when localStorage.slNo3D === '1', when the device has remembered '2D', or when 3D already failed earlier this session. The remembered record is localStorage slIsland3D = {off, why, ver}; it is cleared when SL_WORLD_VER changes or a parent opens ?3d=1. Otherwise it calls loadScript('world/island3d/stage.js?v=N') and then SLIsland3D.boot({ver, deadlineMs: 8000}).
3. boot() runs three things in parallel:
   - window.slLoad3D() for the THREE namespace. It is memoised, and its 15 s timer stays as the outer guard.
   - Exactly two addons, imported with the same Function('s','return import(s)') trick: three/addons/geometries/RoundedBoxGeometry.js and three/addons/utils/BufferGeometryUtils.js (for mergeGeometries).
   - Every island3d script plus world/sound.js and world/music.js, injected at once with async=false so they download in parallel and execute in order. Each file only registers itself into window.SL3D, so load order never affects correctness.
   The whole boot races an 8 s deadline from the moment the island opens. If it misses, boot resolves false and the island stays 2D silently for this visit. A later open in the same session may retry if slLoad3D has resolved by then.
4. The tier is decided BEFORE `new WebGLRenderer`, because antialias can't be changed afterwards: SLTier.decide({ios, android, touch, cores, maxTex, saved}). maxTex comes from a throwaway webgl2 probe context that then calls loseContext().
5. mount() builds the environment and builds templates lazily, only for ids that are actually on the island. It runs renderer.compile(scene, camera) behind a veil and renders the first frame into a canvas at opacity 0, stacked over the SVG. It then crossfades in 300 ms (120 ms under reduced motion) and removes the SVG layer. Target: at most 1.5 s from opening the island to 3D on a cached load.

FALLBACK DETECTION (always silent; the child never sees an error):
- no WebGL2;
- slLoad3D() resolves null;
- an addon import rejects;
- the boot deadline is missed;
- any exception inside boot, mount, sync or a frame (each is wrapped and reported through on.fail);
- webglcontextlost twice in one session. On the first loss: stop, wait for webglcontextrestored, then dispose and remount from the current view model;
- AdaptiveQuality reports fallback (all 5 steps taken and frames still under 20 fps).
On failure, rewards-world disposes the stage, sets use3D=false and redraws the 2D island. Persistent causes (performance, double context loss) also write the remembered-2D record.

SERVICE WORKER:
- cdn.jsdelivr.net is already in the cache-first runtime list (isFont), so three and its addons work offline after the first successful load. They don't need precaching.
- Same-origin: add every new world/ file to APP_SHELL with the same ?v= string as SL_WORLD_VER and bump CACHE_VERSION. Bump both together, as docs §9 already says.
- Photocard PNGs live in Cache Storage 'sl-pc-<LOOK_VERSION>'. Change the activate handler to delete only caches that are neither CACHE_VERSION nor prefixed 'sl-pc-'. Today it deletes every other cache, which would wipe the icons on every deploy.
- Fonts: add Bagel Fat One to the existing Google Fonts link; googleapis and gstatic are already runtime-cached. Before drawing the PET COURSE banner texture, await document.fonts.load with a 1.5 s timeout, falling back to Baloo 2 800 and redrawing the texture once the font arrives.

THIRD PARTIES: no runtime third-party service or plug-in is needed. Three.js from jsDelivr is the only external library, and no physics engine or model files are required. If ElevenLabs Music access arrives, the parent generates the loops offline (an optional tools/gen-music.mjs reading ELEVENLABS_API_KEY from the environment) and commits them as audio/music/*.mp3. The key never ships in the PWA. music.js probes each file once (the service worker caches it) and uses the WebAudio band when a file is missing. Per the user: nothing is deployed. The version bumps are prepared on the rewards-world branch only.
sceneAndCamera:
RENDERER: one per page, owned by stage.js and leased to the island (later to the 3D games).
- new WebGLRenderer({antialias: tier !== 'LOW', alpha: false, stencil: false, powerPreference: 'high-performance'}).
- outputColorSpace SRGBColorSpace; toneMapping NeutralToneMapping; exposure 1.0 by day, 1.08 at Showtime.
- setPixelRatio: LOW 1.0, MID min(dpr, 1.5), HIGH min(dpr, 2); setSize(w, h, false) from the container.
- Shadow map on MID and HIGH only: PCFShadowMap, autoUpdate = false. needsUpdate is set only by the controller after a layout, house-style or land change; changing light intensity never needs it.
- The clear colour is the current fog colour. renderer.info drives the QA stats.

DOM:
- SLIsland3D owns ONE persistent div.slw-3d containing canvas.slw-3dcanvas, div.slw-anchors (HTML labels moved with translate3d), div.slw-focusring and div.slw-camctl (⟲ ⟳ ＋ － ⌂ buttons).
- draw() in rewards-world rebuilds innerHTML often, so drawStage3D() re-parents this container into the new #slwStage. Moving a canvas keeps its GL context, and a ResizeObserver on .slw-3d itself survives the move.
- .slw-stagewrap gets .slw-is3d: no sideways scroll, no fixed 760 px width.
- Stage aspect: 16/9 on landscape and desktop with max-height calc(100vh - 210px); 4/5 on portrait phones with max-height 70vh.
- Canvas touch-action is pan-y in play mode, so the page still scrolls vertically while we receive horizontal drags and pinches. It is none in edit and place modes.

SCENE GRAPH:
- sky: inverted sphere r 90, 24×12, fog false, depthWrite false, renderOrder -10.
- clouds: 4–5 merged-icosphere puffs in one InstancedMesh.
- stars: Points, 250 (LOW 120), sizeAttenuation false, visible when show > 0.
- lights: HemisphereLight, plus DirectionalLight 'sun' at (-7, 14, 9) aimed at (0, 0, 0). Shadow ortho -10..10 × -7..7, near 1, far 40, bias -0.0004, normalBias 0.03, mapSize 1024 (MID) or 2048 (HIGH).
- sea: an 80×80 plane at y -0.32 with the water ShaderMaterial.
- ground: sandTiles, grassTiles, tufts, coveDeco, meadowFlowers, plinths.
- items: one ItemBatch group per (id, stateKey).
- actors: pet rigs, avatar, blob-shadow instances.
- fx: halo pool, particle pool, ground decals, path-runway under-glow.
- cones: 3 additive ConeGeometry(1.3, 10, 16, 1, open) beams. Two sit on decorative stage buoys at the back corners, about (±9.5, -0.32, -6.5); one is on a small light pole behind the house.
- edit: cell outlines and the ghost batch.
- hitRoot, NEVER rendered, holds the raycast boxes and spheres.
- No AmbientLight, PointLight or SpotLight anywhere.

PRESETS: DAY and SHOW are data in world-look.js. env.setShow(k) lerps every value for k in 0..1:
- hemisphere sky/ground colour and intensity (1.9 → 0.85);
- sun → moon colour and intensity (2.4 → 0.9), same direction;
- fog colour, near and far;
- exposure;
- the shared toon uniforms uRimColor and uRimStrength (0.28 → 0.55). The Showtime rim is mix(#FF7AD9, member colour, 0.4);
- the gradient stops for water and sky;
- neon sleeve opacity (0 → 0.45), halo size (1 → 1.6×) and opacity (0.5 → 0.9), star and cone visibility.
The transition takes 1.6 s inOutSine, or a 0.25 s crossfade under reduced motion. The same k drives window glow, fairy-light mode and the path runway.

CAMERA:
- PerspectiveCamera with FOV 30, near 0.5, far 200. up is fixed at (0, 1, 0) and the camera always uses lookAt(target), so it can never roll.
- Rig state {target (x, 0.3, z), yaw, elev, dist, zoom}.
- Default: yaw 0, elev 52°, target = centre of the unlocked land. dist comes from SLGrid3D.fitCamera (bounds including 2.9 u heights, aspect, FOV, elevation, 6% margin). It is recomputed on resize, and on land unlock with a smooth reframe.

CONTROLS (camera.js):
- Mouse drag orbits within yaw ±35° and elevation 40–65°. The wheel zooms 0.75–1.6× with inertia damping 0.12. Right-drag or shift-drag pans, clamped to the land bounds.
- Touch: one-finger horizontal drag = yaw; two fingers = pinch zoom + pan.
- Portrait phones open at fit-width and may zoom to 2.2×, which brings cells to about 44 px. The 2D phone layout used 47 px cells; 2.2× exceeds the bible's 1.6× and needs the art director's sign-off.
- Double-tap on ground or sea dollies toward that point over 0.6 s.
- Long-press (450 ms) on an item frames it and shows its name bubble. This replaces double-tap on items so a toggle act can never fire twice.
- ⌂ resets the view.
- Keyboard: the camera buttons are real buttons. While .slw-camctl has focus, [ and ] rotate, + and - zoom, 0 resets.

MODE CAMERAS:
- Edit and place modes ease to yaw 0, elevation 62° over 0.4 s, so arrow keys always match grid directions. Leaving edit restores the previous view.
- Place mode on phones also zooms to 1.4× and auto-pans to keep the ghost in the central 60%.

REVEAL MOVES (all inOutSine; instant cuts under reduced motion):
- land unlock: crane 52°→40° toward the region over 1.4 s, hold 1.5 s, return over 1.0 s;
- game launch: push in toward the attraction over 0.7 s, then the game shell fades in;
- Showtime: a slow 8° orbit over 8 s and back;
- dance break: a gentle push-in on the house area for the 8 counts.

PROJECTION: camera.project(worldPos) positions the anchor layer on every camera change, and at most 15 Hz while things move.
gridAndPlacement:
MAPPING (grid3d.js, pure):
- 1 cell = 1 u, Y up, +z toward the default camera (row 9 is nearest, like the bottom of the 2D map).
- Cell (c, r) centre = (c - 7.5, surfaceY, r - 4.5).
- An item with fp [w, h] at (x, y) pivots on (x + w/2 - 8, baseY, y + h/2 - 5) and faces +z.
- surfaceY is 0 on Home Island and Beach Cove. Meadow Hill is terraced per column: 0.45 / 0.35 / 0.25 / 0.15 for columns 0 / 1 / 2 / 3. That matches the bible's 0.15→0.45 rise toward the west, and every cell top stays flat.
- baseY = the highest surfaceY across the footprint. If a footprint straddles terraces, env adds a grass plinth slab under it.
- Regions, cells, unlock state, footprints, entrances and occupancy come ONLY from SLWorldCore: REGIONS, REGION_CELLS, unlockedRegions, landSet, fpCells, entranceCells, occupancy, canPlace. The 3D layer never re-implements a rule.
- Organic decor (look.organic: trees, flowers, bushes, rocks, mushrooms) gets yaw ±8° and scale 0.94–1.06 from hash(uid). The house, attractions, paths and fun items are never jittered.
- Models keep a 0.07 u margin on every side, fitting 0.86 × 0.86 per cell. Only tree canopies above y 1.0 may overhang, up to 1.1 u wide.

HIT VOLUMES AND PICKING:
- Every placed item gets an invisible box in hitRoot: fp w × fp h on the ground, height max(look.h, 0.8). Pets and the avatar get 0.4 u-radius spheres, updated just before each raycast. hitRoot.updateMatrixWorld() runs after every sync.
- Raycasting happens only on pointer events, never per frame, and never against render meshes.
- A tap = pointerup within 8 px and 500 ms of pointerdown.
- Pick priority: pet/avatar sphere → nearest item box → locked-land hologram (the ray meets the sea plane where the locked-distance channel is below 0) → ground cell via SLGrid3D.rayToCell. rayToCell marches cell by cell along the ray, testing each cell's top and terrace sides, so meadow cliffs pick correctly.
- Pets and the avatar can't be picked in edit or place mode.

MODES (the state stays in rewards-world; the 3D layer only renders it):
- play: taps go to on.tapItem, tapPet, tapAvatar or tapLand.
- edit: a tap selects the item. Its hull outline turns #FFD23F and pulses 0.018↔0.03 u at 1.5 Hz. Pets sit still. Every unlocked cell shows a white dashed rounded-square outline at 0.55, and the camera tilts to 62°. Dragging an item more than 10 px calls on.dragStart(uid), and rewards-world calls startPlacement(id, uid).
- place: rewards-world passes view.placing = {id, uid, x, y, ok, reason, cells, entrance}, computed with C.canPlace. edit3d then draws:
  - footprint cells #2ECC71 at 0.45 with a Neon Cyan edge when ok;
  - footprint cells #E74C3C at 0.42, pulsing at 1.5 Hz, when not ok;
  - entrance cells #FFD23F at 0.25;
  - every other land cell white dashed.
  The ghost is the item's own template in a ghost batch: same programs, transparent at 0.85, or 0.5 with a grey instance tint when invalid. It is lifted 0.25 u and wobbles ±4° at 3 Hz (it stays still under reduced motion), with its blob shadow at 70% and a gold outline. It may hover over the sea, where its cells read invalid; it is clamped to the 16×10 grid like today's arrow keys.

INPUT PARITY:
- Touch and mouse: tap a cell to move the ghost there; tap the ghost's own cell again while valid to confirm. That is today's rule, now in a factored placeAtCell(x, y). Or drag the ghost and release: on a valid cell this calls confirmPlacement() with today's Undo toast; on an invalid cell it stays in place mode and shows the reason.
- Keyboard: placeKeys is unchanged (arrows move placing.x/y, Enter confirms, Esc cancels, still only while islandOnScreen()). The camera follows the ghost, and the bar message is aria-live.
- Keyboard in play and edit: rewards-world renders ul.slw-sr-list, a visually hidden but focusable list of buttons with today's aria-labels. It covers every interactive item in play mode (every item in edit mode), each pet, the avatar and each lock sign. Focus calls stage.focusItem(uid), which shows a projected #FFD23F focus ring and the gold outline. Enter or Space goes through the same tapItem(uid) path as a canvas tap.

COMMIT:
- Confirm, store and undo still go through commit(), C.place and C.store under navigator.locks.
- The 3D layer animates only after the commit resolves ok:
  - drop-in: fall from 1.2 u in 0.22 s inQuad, squash to y 0.8 / xz 1.12 for 0.08 s, rebound outBack over 0.25 s, 6-puff dust ring, 'chip' + 'pop';
  - store: the item shrinks into a sparkle that flies toward the tray;
  - invalid drop: 'miss' at 0.5 volume.

LOCKED LAND:
- Unlocked regions render real tiles.
- Locked regions are drawn inside the water shader as a translucent #F6E7BD sandbar at sea level, with a dashed Neon Cyan edge and slow scan lines at 0.25, all taken from the locked-distance channel. That costs no extra draw calls.
- The HTML '🔒 name ⭐ price' sign is the same button with the same data-land as today, anchored on the outer edge at SLGrid3D.signAnchor(region). Tapping the hologram does the same as tapping the sign: openItem(land).
- Unlock: cells pop up from the sea in a wave moving out from the home shore, 0.05 s apart, each 0.35 s outBack, with splash rings and sparkles, fanfare + applause and the crane move. The distance field is re-baked at the end. Under reduced motion the land swaps in instantly with a sparkle fade.
modelFactoryApi:
REGISTRATION: each category file is a classic script and never touches a THREE global.
SL3D.defineModels('garden', function (K) { return { tree_oak: { build: fn(ctx) → Template, idle: fn(a), act: fn(a, name) → Act|null, show: fn(a, k) }, … }; });
- stage.js runs every registered factory once THREE is ready, merges the results into SL3D.models, and checks that every LOOK id is covered.
- A missing or throwing builder falls back to K.placeholder(ctx): a rounded slab of the look height in the item's base colour, logged only in QA mode. The controller and the other chunks therefore never block on each other.

ctx GIVEN TO build:
- id;
- look = SLIslandLook.LOOK[id];
- st = the resolved style: {wall, roof, door, details} for the house; {course} for the gate; {ball, stadium} for the pitch; {kart} for the garage; {acc} for pets; {} otherwise;
- stateKey = SLIslandLook.stateKey(id, st);
- tier = 'LOW' | 'MID' | 'HIGH';
- G = the geometry kit bound to that tier;
- col(token) → THREE.Color, resolved only from PALETTE, LOCKED, ART2D or EXTRA.

GEOMETRY KIT G: every builder returns a BufferGeometry with position, normal and a 'color' attribute. uv is dropped, and the geometry is made non-indexed after painting so any mix merges cleanly (Extrude is non-indexed, Lathe is indexed).
- puff(r): Icosahedron detail 1, or a sphere at 12×8 (10×6 on LOW).
- bean(r, len): Capsule 3×10 (2×8 on LOW).
- slab(w, h, d[, radius]): RoundedBox with segments 2 (1 on LOW); radius 0.18 × the smallest side.
- tube(rTop, rBot, h): 12 radial segments (8 on LOW).
- drop(r, h[, 8-point profile]): Lathe with 10 segments (7 on LOW).
- ring(R, r): Torus 16×6 (12×5 on LOW).
- star(rOut, rIn): 5-point Extrude, depth 0.25·rOut, bevel 0.3·depth, 2 bevel segments.
- flag(w, h, sx = 8, sy = 1); ribbon(points, r): CatmullRom tube with 4 radial segments; cone(r, h, radial).
- Helpers:
  - G.t(geo, {p: [x, y, z], r: [deg, deg, deg], s: number | [x, y, z]}) transforms.
  - G.paint(geo, token, tone) with tone = 'base' | 'shade' | 'hi' (±12% lightness).
  - G.paintBy(geo, fn(vertex) → token) for stripes and wedges.
  - G.facet(geo) bakes flat normals, which avoids a separate flatShading program.
  - G.merge([...]).

TEMPLATE, built with K.template(ctx):
- .part(name, geos[], matKey, {pivot, perCopy, castShadow, outline, stateColor, receiveShadow = true})
- .pivot(name, origin [x, y, z], parent)
- .anchor(name, [x, y, z]): 'top' for labels and emotes; also 'door', 'seat', 'spot'…
- .hit([w, h, d]): defaults come from the look.
- .done() → a frozen Template {parts, pivots, anchors, hit, height, tris}. It merges the geometries of each part. In QA mode it warns when an item has more than 4 static materials, more than 6 parts, or more tris than look.tris. castShadow is honoured only on static parts.

MATERIAL KEYS (shared; K creates each once):
- 'toon': MeshToonMaterial with vertexColors and a 4×1 RedFormat ramp [110, 165, 215, 255] with Nearest filtering. The rim patch goes before <opaque_fragment>. All toon materials share ONE uniforms object, and customProgramCacheKey is 'encore-toon'.
- 'gold' | 'chrome' | 'pearl': MeshMatcapMaterial with 128² matcaps drawn at runtime.
- 'glass': pearl, transparent at 0.45, depthWrite false.
- 'neon:<Token>': MeshBasic with toneMapped false.
- 'glow:<Token>': the additive sleeve; its opacity follows the Showtime mix k.
- 'state': MeshBasic using vertex colour × instance colour, for lantern glass, mushroom caps, windows and bulbs. Lit or unlit is an instance colour, never a rebuild.
- 'ink'.
- Outline hulls: the batch generates them for parts with outline: true, on MID and HIGH only. BackSide basic in #3B2F4A, normal push uOutline 0.018 u for buildings and 0.012 u for characters. The selected copy's instance colour turns gold.

CACHING:
- K.templates.get(id, stateKey, tier) memoises Templates.
- K.parts.get(key, tier, fn) memoises sub-parts: each roof, door, detail, accessory and kart body. A house restyle therefore assembles from cache in under 2 ms.
- Geometries are shared between batches and the photocard renderer. stage.dispose() disposes everything, and the cache is trimmed LRU-style beyond 120 templates.

INSTANCING, via K.batch(template) → ItemBatch:
- Every placed item, unique or repeatable, lives in a batch keyed by (id, stateKey): one InstancedMesh per part, capacity 4 and doubling as needed.
- instanceColor is always allocated, so every static item shares ONE toon program.
- API:
  - add(uid, {x, y, fp}, {jitter}), move(uid, x, y), remove(uid) (swaps with the last instance);
  - hide(uid) / show(uid), used while the item is the ghost;
  - setState(uid, key, value);
  - setHighlight(uid, 0 none | 1 focus | 2 selected);
  - pivot(uid, name) → the Matrix4 to write;
  - commit().
- Static parts are written once, on add or move, and never touched again. Pivoted parts are rewritten only while their idle or act runs.
- perCopy parts (flag cloth, bunting pennants, cape) become one plain Mesh per copy, so each copy's CPU vertex wave can differ.
- Paths and multi-copy decor therefore cost one draw call per part however many are placed.

ANIMATION HANDLE a, passed to idle, act and show:
- Context: uid, t, dt, phase (0..1 from the uid hash), rand (seeded by uid), reduced, beat (0..1 within the current beat), bar, bpm, show (0..1).
- pivot(name).set(rotDeg[], pos[], scale[]) and state(key, value).
- halo(name, on, sizeU, token) and decal(on, token).
- emit(kind, anchorOrLocalPos, n, opts).
- sfx(name, vol, step), panned automatically by the item's x.
- pets: {active(), perform(kind, uid)}.
- shake(amp, dur) and squish().
Act = {dur, update(a, tAct) → alive, cancel()}. The controller guarantees one live act per uid: a new tap restarts it and never stacks a second. It calls the reduced variant when a.reduced is set. Every tap first runs the universal squish (1 → 0.92 → 1.06 → 1 over 0.25 s) with 'pop'.

STYLE VARIANTS:
- house: stateKey = 'wall|roof|door|d:<sorted details>'; detail_flag is dropped when roof_castle is selected. The body uses the LOCKED WALL colour with 6%-darker skirting. The door uses the LOCKED DOOR colour, or the GOLD matcap for door_gold. The roof and each detail are sub-parts. Any change produces a new stateKey: the house batch swaps template, the shadow map gets needsUpdate, and a debut sparkle plays.
- att_course: stateKey = the selected course (THEME colours plus that variant's dressing).
- att_pitch: stateKey = ball|stadium.
- att_kart: stateKey = kart; the half-scale parked kart comes from the shared kart builder.

KARTS: SL3D.make('kart_<x>', {}, tier) builds the 0.9 u kart in its LOCKED KARTS colour, with a 'seat' socket and a neon under-glow strip:
- blue: white rocket stripes and fins;
- lime: #FFD23F bolt decals;
- unicorn: gold horn and rainbow-mane spoiler;
- gold: GOLD matcap with star decals.

PETS: SL3D.makeRig(petId, acc, tier) → PetRig {root, bones{body, head, neck, tail, earL, earR, legs×4, wingL, wingR}, sockets{hat, neck, face, back, seat}, setPose(pose), setShow(k), dispose()}.
- Rigid skinning: one SkinnedMesh per material, with each vertex bound 100% to one bone. A pet wearing accessories costs at most 3 draw calls plus its outline.
- Accessories are sub-parts with a socket name. The cape is perCopy CPU cloth on the 'back' socket, and its wave grows with speed. The shades switch to PEARL when show > 0.5.

SHARED USE: photocards and the 3D games use the same make and makeRig (the pet as course runner, penalty kicker and kart driver).
animation:
PRINCIPLES:
- The island clock is the music beat clock, SLMusic.clock() → {bpm, t0}. When music is off, an internal clock runs at the same tempo: 100 BPM by day, 118 at Showtime.
- Idle periods are multiples of half a beat where the bible allows it.
- Every loop takes its phase from hash(uid), so nothing marches in lockstep except the dance.
- Nothing flashes or strobes faster than 2 Hz (wings and tails excepted). A look/motion test enforces this.
- Only animated instances get matrix writes each frame. The controller keeps a 'ticking' set: idle-animated batches in view, live acts, actors and particles.

PETS WANDERING (pets-brain.js is pure; actors.js applies it):
- Free cells = unlocked land minus 'object'-layer occupancy. Paths and entrance cells are walkable. Only the trampoline and bench acts ever put a pet on an occupied cell.
- Planning: A* over 8 neighbours with no corner cutting, Catmull-Rom smoothing through cell centres, speed 0.9 u/s, turn rate 6 rad/s.
- Each pet reserves its target cell, so two pets never pick the same spot or overlap.
- On every sync the brain re-plans any pet whose cell or path became blocked. A fully enclosed pet pops to the nearest free cell with a sparkle.
- Gaits:
  - puppy: trot, tail wag 1.5 Hz (4 Hz when happy);
  - kitten: S-tail sway, an occasional pounce;
  - bunny: 0.18 u hops;
  - dragon: flutters 0.12 u above the ground, wings at 3 Hz while moving.
- An idle action every 4–8 s: sit, sniff, look at the camera, scratch, roll over; the bunny's ear flops now and then.
- Tap: a happy hop, an emote sprite (heart, note or star) and the pet's voice.
- In edit and place modes pets sit where they are.
- Each actor has a blob shadow that shrinks as it rises.
- Reduced motion: pets stand still at their spots and only turn and emote.

AVATAR:
- A chibi bean in the child's member colour, with their emoji on a 128² face texture.
- Stands on the left half of the house's entrance cell, which the rules keep free of objects.
- Bobs 0.02 u at 0.5 Hz and glances at a pet every ~6 s. Holds the Island Wand at Showtime.
- Tap: wave plus finger-heart (pink heart sprite and 'pop').

IDLE LOOPS (per the bible):
- Trees sway as a whole-instance rotation about the base: oak, apple and blossom 1.5° every 4.2 s; pine 1° every 5 s; palm 3° every 3.6 s.
- Flower heads bob ±2% every 2.4 s. Sunflower heads track the sun by day and the sweeping spotlight at Showtime.
- The mossy rock blinks every 5–9 s.
- Flags and bunting flutter: a CPU sine on the per-copy cloth, 0.04 u at 2 Hz, growing toward the free edge.
- Windmill 0.25 rev/s. Fountain: 3 idle droplet arcs (12 instanced drops). Chimney: 3 smoke puffs on a 2.4 s loop.
- Fairy lights twinkle by day and chase on the beat at Showtime, never faster than 2 Hz.
- Bubble machine: 1 bubble every 2 s. Blossom petals: at most 40 on the island. The snowman's 6 sparkles drift around him.
- Lit lanterns and mushrooms pulse ±12% on the beat while music plays.
- Sea bands scroll at 0.04 u/s; clouds drift at 0.08 u/s; stars twinkle in the shader.
- Reduced motion: no sway, bob or petals; chase lights become a steady glow.

INTERACTIVE ITEMS (act handlers): each act lasts at most 3 s (the swing's decay is the exception), can be interrupted, and never stacks.
- trampoline: the active pet runs over (≤ 1.2 s) and does 3 bounces of 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0 u with a front flip on the last. The mat dips 0.12 u at each contact. 'boing' ×3 with combo 0/2/4.
- fountain: a 3 s concert show (centre, left, right, then all together), with neon droplet tints at Showtime. 'whoosh', combo 0–3, then 'star'.
- swing: pendulum to ±38°, period 1.6 s, decaying over 4 s; 'whoosh' at the first 3 high points.
- bubbles: 24 PEARL bubbles rise 1.5–3 u, wobbling, and pop with a sparkle; 'pop' for at most 6, with the combo stepping up.
- lantern, mushrooms, lighthouse ('glow'): 3 gentle flicker steps over 0.25 s, then on, with a halo and, at Showtime, a ground light pool. 'star' when switched on, 'chip' when switched off.
- lighthouse beams rotate at 0.3 rev/s, warm by day; at Showtime they cycle pink → cyan → violet every 4 s.
- windmill: spins up to 2.5 rev/s and eases back over 3 s; 'whoosh' plus 'boost' at 0.4.
- flag: flutters harder (0.12 u) for 1.2 s. Bunting: a left-to-right ripple in 0.6 s.
- house door: swings open 70° in 0.3 s with 3 hearts, 'pop' + 'unlock'; it closes when the style sheet closes.
- course gate, garage, pitch ('launch'): spotlights snap to it at Showtime, a sparkle ring by day, then 'whoosh' and a 0.7 s push-in before the game opens.
- garage kart: revs with a 3 Hz wobble, 2 pastel exhaust puffs, 'boost'.
- Decor with no act still squishes with 'pop'.

CELEBRATIONS:
- Placement drop-in: falls from 1.2 u in 0.22 s (inQuad), squashes to y 0.8 / xz 1.12 for 0.08 s, rebounds outBack over 0.25 s; 6-puff dust ring; 'chip' + 'pop'.
- New purchase: debuts on the photocard riser with one 360° turn over 1.2 s and a sparkle burst; 'coins' then 'tada'. At 300 ⭐ or more, confetti cannons fire from both screen edges with 'fanfare'.
- Land unlock: the land rises, 3 sparkle-ring fireworks, applause.
- ENCORE: Showtime runs for 8 s after a purchase, a land unlock or a goal. It starts when the celebration card closes, so the child sees it. 'sting' + 'whoosh' on, 'chip' off.
- DANCE BREAK, every 16 bars while Showtime is on. Pets first walk (at most 2 s) to open cells near the house, then 8 counts at 118 BPM (~4.07 s):
  - counts 1–2: side-steps with a 10° lean;
  - counts 3–4: two hops;
  - counts 5–6: signature moves (puppy tail-wag shuffle, kitten paw point, bunny hop-spin, dragon wing twirl with a sparkle puff, avatar wand wave);
  - count 7: everyone faces the camera;
  - count 8: group pose with finger-hearts and a sparkle burst; 'cheer' at the end.
  Under reduced motion it is one group pose with a sparkle fade.
- Confetti: hearts, stars and rectangles plus curly streamers, 40% in the member colour, at most 120 alive. Reduced motion turns it into a 0.4 s sparkle fade.
- No full-screen white flash in any mode.
performance:
TIERS (tier.js decides before the renderer exists; the result is saved per device in try/catch):
- LOW: iOS or Android with hardwareConcurrency ≤ 4, or MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE < 8192, or a saved LOW.
- HIGH: a desktop without touch and with ≥ 8 cores.
- MID: everything else.
iPadOS reports itself as a Mac, so detect it with maxTouchPoints > 1. Safari may clamp hardwareConcurrency, so the saved measured tier and the adaptive ladder are the real safety net.

ISLAND BUDGETS (LOW / MID / HIGH):
| | LOW | MID | HIGH |
|---|---|---|---|
| draw calls | ≤ 70 | ≤ 100 | ≤ 150 |
| triangles | ≤ 60k | ≤ 120k | ≤ 200k |
| particles | 128 | 256 | 512 |
| pixel ratio | 1.0 | min(dpr, 1.5) | min(dpr, 2) |
| shadows | none | 1024² | 2048² |
| outlines | off | on | on |
| bloom | never | never | optional |
Bloom on HIGH means UnrealBloomPass at half resolution, only after ≥ 55 fps has been measured.
Estimates: the starter island is about 25 calls and 18k tris. A maxed island (all land, every placeable id, many copies, 4 pets) is about 75 calls on MID and 65 on LOW, because each id costs 1–2 calls however many copies are placed.

HOW:
1. Vertex-colour toon: palette colours are baked into the geometry, so every toon part shares ONE material and program. An item is usually one toon call, plus the occasional matcap, neon or state call.
2. Every placed item lives in an InstancedMesh batch per (id, stateKey), always with instanceColor allocated, so all static items share one program. Static matrices are written once.
3. Pets and the avatar are rigid-skinned SkinnedMeshes, at most 3 calls each.
4. One InstancedMesh each for halos (camera-facing billboard shader), particles (sprite atlas), blob shadows and cell outlines.
5. The water shader also draws the foam, the day glints, the locked-land hologram and its neon dashes.
6. Ground tiles are an instanced chamfered tile geometry with no bottom face, about 44 tris each, so about 10k tris for all 111 land cells. Alternate grass tiles are offset 0.001 u to avoid z-fighting.
7. The shadow map is static (autoUpdate false); needsUpdate is set only after layout, style or land changes.
8. LOW cuts segment counts by about 30%, drops outlines and the shadow map (blob shadows only) and halves the star count.

SHADER PROGRAMS: at most 12 on LOW and at most 16 on MID/HIGH (shadow-depth and outline variants), checked with renderer.info.programs. Rules that keep the count down:
- no flatShading define (G.facet bakes faceted normals instead);
- receiveShadow true on every toon item;
- no textures on toon materials;
- instanceColor on every batch;
- fog on everything except the sky.
renderer.compile runs behind the veil. A template that appears for the first time is compiled off-screen before its debut.

TEXTURES: all generated on canvas at runtime, under 8 MB of GPU memory:
- toon ramp 4×1;
- halo, blob and sparkle atlas cells at 64² each;
- 4 matcaps at 128²;
- 1 emoji face at 128²;
- PET COURSE banner 512×128;
- shore/locked field 64×40 (two channels, RG);
- LED board 256×64, animated by UV offset and never redrawn per frame.

CPU:
- View update ≤ 4 ms per frame on the target iPad.
- Zero allocations in the frame loop: each module keeps scratch Vector3, Matrix4, Quaternion and Color objects.
- Raycast only on pointer events, against hit volumes.
- Anchors are re-projected only on a camera change, or at most 15 Hz while things move.
- Templates are built lazily on first use and cached. The land and shore field are re-baked only on unlock.

PACING (stage.js + SLTier.FramePacer):
- setAnimationLoop, capped at 60 fps on 120 Hz screens.
- 30 fps after 20 s without input; back to 60 on the next input.
- Render nothing while:
  - document.hidden is true;
  - the island tab is hidden (onHide);
  - less than 10% of the stage is in view (IntersectionObserver);
  - a sheet, celebration or game covers it (setCovered);
  - reduced motion is on and nothing is animating (render on demand only).

ADAPTIVE QUALITY:
- Track a rolling 120-frame average of work time (update + render CPU) and of frame intervals.
- A steady ~33 ms cadence with low variance is treated as a 30 Hz cap (iOS Low Power Mode), not as slowness.
- If the averages imply more than 24 ms per frame for 2 s, step down once per 2 s: pixel ratio -0.25 → shadows off → outlines off → particle caps halved → Showtime cones off.
- Never step back up within a session.
- After all steps, sustained frame rates under 20 fps, or two context losses, switch to 2D for the session and remember it.

MEMORY:
- Suspend on hide; dispose after 30 s hidden or on pagehide.
- A profile switch reuses the renderer but drops the actor rigs and the emoji texture.
- The photocard renderer is a separate small context, created only while its queue or a turntable is active and force-lost when idle.
- Leak check in the lab: renderer.info.memory geometries and textures return to baseline after 20 mount/sync/dispose cycles.

Checklist, LOW tier first:
- Screen sizes: a 375×812 phone, a 768×1024 iPad and a desktop, each in Day and Showtime.
- Every item is recognisable beside its neighbours at the 52° view and at 48 px in the shop.

workBreakdown.chunk: 1. Pure foundations: look table, grid maths, motion timelines (wave 1)
workBreakdown.details: Transcribe the art bible into LOOK for all 81 ids. Schema: {h, kind, colors{part: token}, pivots[], actPivot, idle{type, deg|pct, period}, show{neon[], halo, led, chase}, organic, outline, instancing:'batch', hit[w,h,d], tris}. Tokens may come only from PALETTE, LOCKED, ART2D or EXTRA. Also write the DAY/SHOW presets, TEMPO, shineLevel and stateKey. Implement grid3d and motion as pure UMD modules exposing the globals SLIslandLook, SLGrid3D and SLMotion; no THREE, no DOM. Commit the API surface (function names and signatures in the file headers) first, so every other chunk can code against it. This chunk is the only one allowed to change the LOOK schema.

workBreakdown.chunk: 2. Runtime core: tiers, stage/loader, kit and materials (wave 1)
workBreakdown.details: stage.js: SLIsland3D.boot (three + 2 addons via the import map, a parallel async=false script loader, the 8 s deadline, the WebGL2 check, the remembered-2D record), the SL3D.defineModels registry with coverage check and placeholder fallback, renderer creation per tier, a lease API for later game use, the setAnimationLoop pacer, pauses (hidden / IntersectionObserver / covered), context lost and restored, the adaptive-quality runtime, dispose. kit.js: the K API exactly as specified under modelFactoryApi: G primitives bound to the tier, paint/facet/merge with attribute normalisation, the material set with the shared toon rim uniforms, outline hull, matcap and canvas texture generators, Template, ItemBatch (instanceColor always on, pivot writes, perCopy parts, outline instances), template and part caches, placeholder, and base classes for billboard, blob and particle pools. Owns the K contract; other chunks request changes rather than editing it.

workBreakdown.chunk: 3. Environment: ground, sea, sky, light presets, locked land
workBreakdown.details: Instanced chamfered grass/sand tiles from SLWorldCore.REGION_CELLS for unlocked regions; checker tint with 0.001 u offset; meadow terraces and plinths; cove sand with shells and starfish; wildflowers; tufts. The water ShaderMaterial uses the grid3d two-channel field (foam band, wave lines, day glints, Showtime colours and spot streaks, plus the locked-land sandbar, neon dashes and scan lines). Sky dome, cloud puffs, star Points, stage buoys, 3 spotlight cones, hemisphere light and sun/moon with the static shadow camera, fog, env.setShow(k) driven by the world-look presets, and env.riseRegion(region) → animation handle. Polish the sea and its foam ring first. Depends on chunks 1 and 2 (API only).

workBreakdown.chunk: 4. Models: garden, lights, flags, landmarks, paths
workBreakdown.details: Registers tree_oak, tree_pine, tree_apple, tree_blossom, tree_palm, flower_tulip, flower_daisy, flower_sun, bush_rose, rock_mossy, lantern, mushroom_glow, flag_pole, bunting, bench, sandcastle, umbrella, snowman, windmill, lighthouse, path_stone, path_wood and path_flower. Each gets build, idle, act and show handlers to the bible's heights, colours, triangle budgets and pivots. Lantern and mushroom lit state uses the 'state' material plus instance colour. Flag and bunting cloth are perCopy CPU waves. Windmill sails are a pivoted part with Showtime light-painting tips. Lighthouse beams cycle colours at Showtime only. Paths carry the runway under-glow that fx/island3d chase. Uses K and SLMotion only.

house_cottage is assembled from cached sub-parts. Body with LOCKED walls and skirting, step and doormat; windows with ink muntins that glow at Showtime; 4 doors (gold = matcap with 2 glints every 4 s); roofs red, blue, thatch, candy and castle, each with a distinct silhouette; details windowbox, chimney with smoke, fairy lights (11 bulbs, twinkle, beat chase ≤ 2 Hz) and rooftop flag (hidden with castle). The door act swings open 70° and back. Outline on MID and HIGH. Stays under 3,500 tris with every detail. Exposes the anchors 'door', 'top' and 'spot'.

trampoline (the mat pivot dips; asks the actors API, a.pets.perform('trampoline', uid), for the pet's bounces), fountain (2-tier lathe basin, rippling water, 12 instanced drops, the 3 s concert jet sequence from SLMotion), swing (A-frame with leafy bar; the seat on a 'swing' pivot with the pendulum and decay), bubbles (machine, wand; emits PEARL bubbles through a.emit). Bump SL_WORLD_VER and the ?v= strings together. Update the docs. Do NOT deploy or push (per the user); commit on the rewards-world branch only when asked. Can start in parallel by coding against the documented SLIsland3D API, since the 2D path keeps working while the stage is absent.

A dev harness that loads the same scripts as the app (world-core, world-art, world-look, island3d/*, sound, music) with fixtures: starter, max island, showcase, ?item=<id>; tier, Day/Showtime, reduced-motion and wireframe toggles; a stats panel with budget assertions; a context-loss button; a fallback simulation; a memory-cycle test. Not linked from the app and not precached. Run the visual checklist in the testing section with the Browser pane at mobile, tablet and desktop sizes; report screenshots and budget numbers per tier back to the owners of chunks 3–11.

risks: Gestures on phones: a one-finger horizontal orbit under touch-action pan-y can feel inconsistent, and young children may rotate the island while trying to tap. Mitigations: 8 px tap slop, tight yaw clamps, the ⌂ reset and camera buttons. If testing shows confusion, turn one-finger orbit off on phones and use the buttons only.

Readability on portrait phones: at fit-width the 16-column island gives about 22 px cells. Comfortable editing needs zoom up to 2.2× plus panning, which exceeds the bible's 1.6×. The art director needs to approve this.

Older iPads: limited GPU memory, and Safari drops WebGL contexts when the app is backgrounded or two contexts (island + photocards) are alive. Suspend, dispose and remount covers this, but it must be proven on a real device.

Safari may clamp or misreport navigator.hardwareConcurrency, so tiers can be misdetected. iOS Low Power Mode caps rAF at 30 Hz, which looks like slowness. The adaptive controller measures work time and recognises a steady 30 Hz cadence; the tier saved per device fixes later sessions.

Shader programs can creep past 12 (instancing, skinning, shadow-depth and outline variants). The unification rules and a measured cap (12 on LOW, 16 on MID/HIGH) are needed, and the bible's '≤ 12' target is only fully met on LOW.

draw() rewrites innerHTML after every commit. If any path recreates the canvas instead of re-parenting the persistent container, it leaks GL contexts and stutters. The lab cycle test must cover 20 draw cycles.

BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries throws when indexed and non-indexed geometries are mixed (Extrude vs Lathe/Sphere) or attribute sets differ. The kit must normalise every geometry; a missed case breaks a whole builder (the placeholder fallback hides it, so check the QA logs).
Coplanar overlapping grass tiles in alternating checker colours will z-fight without the 0.001 u offset. The 1.5 u sand tiles overlap at one height but share a colour, so they're safe.

The 2D fallback and the 3D look can drift. Locked colours are test-enforced but shapes are not. Photocard PNGs are cached by LOOK_VERSION, which must be bumped on every look change. Without the sw.js activate change, all icons are wiped and re-rendered on every deploy.

The bible's 'double-tap an item to dolly in' conflicts with single-tap acts (a lantern would toggle twice), so this plan uses long-press to frame items. That is a deliberate deviation to confirm with the art director.

Celebration sequencing: the full-screen celebration card would hide the land rising and the drop-in. Play the 3D moment first (skippable), then show the card, then start the encore. Otherwise the 3D effort is invisible.

Text in textures: the PET COURSE banner needs Bagel Fat One loaded before it is drawn. Emoji faces render differently by OS, and some emoji are missing on older Android. Use font-wait timeouts, a redraw once the font arrives, and a 🙂 fallback.

Accessibility: the canvas is invisible to screen readers and the keyboard. The hidden focusable list, the anchors and the aria-live bar must stay in sync with sync(). Placement arrows rely on edit mode forcing yaw 0.

Renderer sharing with the 3D games: if the games plan creates its own renderer instead of using stage.js lease(), older iPads end up with duplicate shader compiles and a second large context. Coordinate the lease API early.

First-open download: three r170 minified (about 0.7 MB) plus about 18 small scripts can miss the 8 s deadline on slow connections. The child then stays on 2D for that visit; the next visit loads from the service-worker cache.

Parallel-build contracts: the LOOK schema (chunk 1) and the K/Template/ItemBatch/PetRig APIs (chunks 2 and 8) are the integration seams. Mid-build changes there break other chunks, so only their owners may change them, through a change note. Every other file registers only its own SL3D keys.

K-pop compliance: everything is original (generic neon, glow wands shaped as star bulbs, generic dance moves, instrumental music prompts without artist names). A reviewer should still check that no colour pair, wand silhouette or choreography accidentally resembles a real fandom's; member colours come from the existing u.color only.

No deploy (per the user's request). All version bumps (SL_WORLD_VER, ?v= strings, CACHE_VERSION) are prepared on the rewards-world branch and must not be pushed to main or mirrored until the parent says so.
